cards.back: The layer of gases around Earth.
cards.say: atmosphere. The layer of gases around Earth.

cards.front: Is air a single gas or a mixture of gases?
cards.back: A mixture of gases.
cards.say: Is air a single gas or a mixture of gases? A mixture of gases.

cards.back: The gas that makes up most of the air, about 78 per cent.
cards.say: nitrogen. The gas that makes up most of the air, about 78 per cent.

cards.back: The gas in the air that living things breathe and that things need to burn. It makes up about 21 per cent of the air.
cards.say: oxygen. The gas in the air that living things breathe and that things need to burn. It makes up about 21 per cent of the air.

cards.back: A gas that makes up a tiny part of the air, about 0.04 per cent. Plants take it in and animals breathe it out.
cards.say: carbon dioxide. A gas that makes up a tiny part of the air, about 0.04 per cent. Plants take it in and animals breathe it out.

cards.front: Where does the water vapour in the air come from?
cards.back: It evaporates from seas, lakes, rivers and wet ground.
cards.say: Where does the water vapour in the air come from? It evaporates from seas, lakes, rivers and wet ground.

cards.front: Is natural water, such as river water, pure?
cards.back: No. It contains dissolved minerals and gases and tiny pieces of solid.
cards.say: Is natural water, such as river water, pure? No. It contains dissolved minerals and gases and tiny pieces of solid.

cards.back: Water with nothing else mixed in it.
cards.say: pure water. Water with nothing else mixed in it.

cards.front: Is clear water always safe to drink?
cards.back: No. It may still have germs or dissolved chemicals in it.
cards.say: Is clear water always safe to drink? No. It may still have germs or dissolved chemicals in it.

cards.back: It is filtered to remove solids, and chlorine is added to kill germs.
cards.say: How is drinking water cleaned? It is filtered to remove solids, and chlorine is added to kill germs.

cards.back: Harmful substances added to the air, water or land.
cards.say: pollution. Harmful substances added to the air, water or land.

cards.back: Smoke, dust and harmful gases in the air, for example from vehicles and factories.
cards.say: air pollution. Smoke, dust and harmful gases in the air, for example from vehicles and factories.

cards.back: Rubbish, sewage, oil or chemicals in rivers, lakes and seas.
cards.say: water pollution. Rubbish, sewage, oil or chemicals in rivers, lakes and seas.

cards.back: Litter, waste and chemicals dumped on the land.
cards.say: land pollution. Litter, waste and chemicals dumped on the land.

cards.front: What is a major cause of air pollution?
cards.back: Burning fuels such as petrol, diesel and coal.
cards.say: What is a major cause of air pollution? Burning fuels such as petrol, diesel and coal.

cards.front: How does an oil spill harm sea birds?
cards.back: The oil coats their feathers, so they cannot fly or keep warm.
cards.say: How does an oil spill harm sea birds? The oil coats their feathers, so they cannot fly or keep warm.

cards.back: Rain made acidic by gases from burning fuels. It harms trees, fish and buildings.
cards.say: acid rain. Rain made acidic by gases from burning fuels. It harms trees, fish and buildings.

cards.front: How can fertiliser washed into a river harm fish?
cards.back: It makes algae grow too fast. When the algae die, bacteria use up the oxygen in the water.
cards.say: How can fertiliser washed into a river harm fish? It makes algae grow too fast. When the algae die, bacteria use up the oxygen in the water.

cards.front: How does carbon dioxide from burning fuels affect Earth?
cards.back: It traps heat in the atmosphere and makes Earth warmer.
cards.say: How does carbon dioxide from burning fuels affect Earth? It traps heat in the atmosphere and makes Earth warmer.

cards.back: Walk, cycle or use buses, recycle, put litter in bins and use less energy.
cards.say: Name ways to reduce pollution. Walk, cycle or use buses, recycle, put litter in bins and use less energy.

cards.back: To use old materials to make new things, instead of throwing them away.
cards.say: recycle. To use old materials to make new things, instead of throwing them away.

cards.front: Why is plastic in the sea a danger to animals?
cards.back: Animals can eat it by mistake or get tangled up in it.
cards.say: Why is plastic in the sea a danger to animals? Animals can eat it by mistake or get tangled up in it.

cards.front: How do plants help keep the air fresh?
cards.back: They take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.
cards.say: How do plants help keep the air fresh? They take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.

cards.front: How can you test if a water sample is pure?
cards.back: Evaporate it. Pure water leaves nothing behind, but impure water leaves a solid residue.
cards.say: How can you test if a water sample is pure? Evaporate it. Pure water leaves nothing behind, but impure water leaves a solid residue.
